findings.issue: ClientIp trusts the leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry, but nothing overwrites it: services/gateway has no filter that strips or rewrites the header, Spring Cloud Gateway's XForwardedHeadersFilter appends, RateLimitWebFilter.remoteIp (lines 130-157) documents that left entries can be forged, and values.yaml sets trustedProxyHops: 2 (CloudFront + ALB append). Any client through the normal gateway path controls entry 0: (a) bypass REFERRAL_IP_MATCH with one header; (b) REFERRAL_IP_MATCH becomes an oracle for whether a referrer used an arbitrary IP in the last 30 days (refusals do not consume the claim); (c) unbounded activity rows by rotating the header.
findings.fix: Select the client entry like the gateway: N entries from the RIGHT with a configurable trusted-hop count (gateway trustedProxyHops + 1 for the gateway's own append), falling back to remoteAddr when N=0 or too few entries; or have the gateway drop inbound XFF and forward one trusted header. Test that 'spoofed, real-client, alb, gateway' resolves to real-client and a spoofed left entry cannot cause or avoid a match. Correct CEO assumption 3 and the auth-service application.yml comment (lines 312-315) that also claims the gateway overwrites XFF.

findings.issue: REFERRAL_IP_MATCH and REFERRAL_CODE_TOO_NEW are distinct 422s that reveal referrer facts; refusals do not consume the slot, so they can be probed. After the major fix the leak is limited to the claimant's own real IP.
findings.fix: Accept and document as residual risk; optionally one shared refusal code or a per-referee refusal rate limit.

findings.issue: recordActivity upserts one row per distinct (user, ip_hash) with no per-user cap.
findings.fix: Cap rows kept per user (e.g. most recent 20), deleting older ones in the same statement.

findings.issue: The IPv6 literal guard accepts strings starting with '.', e.g. '.:1', which InetAddress hands to the resolver: a DNS/hosts lookup from attacker input despite the no-DNS design.
findings.fix: Require the first character to be a hex digit or ':', or use a resolver-free parser; add '.:1' and '..:' to ClientIpTest.

findings.issue: Any non-blank salt is accepted as the HMAC key however short; a weak salt plus a leaked users schema allows offline brute force of IPv4.
findings.fix: Under TD-P8-24, WARN (or fail in prod) for salts shorter than 32 bytes; document a generation command.

summary: Request changes. Authn, SQL binding, PII handling, HMAC keying, retention, deletion and the claim race are sound. Blocking: the client-IP trust model. ClientIp uses the leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry, which the caller controls because the gateway appends rather than overwrites and CloudFront and the ALB sit in front (trustedProxyHops=2). Any client can bypass the IP check, use REFERRAL_IP_MATCH as an oracle for arbitrary IPs, and add unbounded activity rows. Select the right-hand entry with a configurable trusted-hop count matching RateLimitWebFilter and add a spoofing test. The auth-service comment claiming the gateway overwrites X-Forwarded-For is also wrong (outside this diff). (Stored verbatim in substance by the CEO.)
